Subject: Audit logging - SOC 2 / vendor questionnaire follow-up

Hi Tom / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — great to meet a few folks from Acme's security team. Quick recap from our discovery call and next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) SOC 2 status: we confirmed Redwood is currently in the middle of our SOC 2 Type II audit cycle; Type I completed in 2025 and Type II expected Q4 2026. We can share interim evidence and the SOC 2 scope doc.

2) GDPR / HIPAA: Redwood supports data processing agreements and signed BAA where required. We do not process PHI on our hosted plan without a signed BAA; Private deployments can be configured for HIPAA workloads.

3) Vendor security questionnaire: attached is a partially completed copy of your questionnaire (Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_ACME.xlsx). Please flag any items you want completed first.

4) Audit logging (details requested): see attached spec (Redwood_Audit_Logging_Specs.pdf) — highlights below:
   - Admin activity logs: IAM changes, role grants/revocations, console and API admin actions; events include actor, timestamp, IP, resource affected.
   - API logs: per-request logs include request id, model id/version, prompt length, tokens in/out, response latencies; we capture headers and routing decisions for debugging.
   - Exportability: logs can be exported to customer S3 (parquet/JSON), streamed to a customer SIEM via syslog or kinesis, or pulled via secure APIs.
   - Immutability & tamper-evidence: write-once logs with append-only storage (object versioning on S3) + checksums; for Private we offer WORM configurations.
   - Retention & deletion: configurable retention per-account; export before purge; retention policies support legal hold for e-discovery.

Next steps (proposed):
- I will send the completed questionnaire sections on scope / access controls by EOD Monday (Jul 20).
- Aditya (cc'd) can schedule a short technical call to demo the audit logs export (30 min).
- If helpful, we can provide limited-scope temporary read access to a logging demo for your security reviewers.

Attachments: Redwood_Audit_Logging_Specs.pdf (2 pages), Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_ACME.xlsx (partial)

Thanks,

Marissa Cole

Marissa — thanks for the comprehensive recap. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the spec: 

- Immutability: can you clarify the mechanism for tamper-evidence on the hosted offering? Is that guaranteed via S3 object versioning + checksums, or do you maintain an append-only ledger within Redwood as well? We need assurance for our compliance team that logs cannot be retroactively altered.

- Export frequency: what is the near-real-time latency for streaming logs to a SIEM? Our SOC team needs ~1–2 minute latency for admin events.

- Retention controls: will we be able to set retention at the workspace level and apply legal-hold exceptions per dataset?

Also, attaching a couple of priority questions we need answered in the vendor questionnaire (see attached). Can we aim to have your answers by end of week? If not, let's lock a 30-min follow-up call.

Thanks — Tom

Tom — great questions, answered inline and proposing timing below.

- Immutability: for hosted customers we use a combination of S3 object versioning + write-once retention buckets for exported logs, plus checksum-based verification and a ledger that records export/rotation operations. While we don't expose a blockchain ledger, the combination provides tamper-evidence: any change to an exported log archive changes the checksum and object versions. For Private deployments we can support WORM (Write Once Read Many) storage at the bucket level per your policy.

- Export frequency / latency: streaming to SIEM via our Kafka/Kinesis connector is typically sub-60s for admin events in our staging tests; 1–2 minute SLA is achievable with dedicated throughput (we can size accordingly on Dedicated or Private).

- Retention controls: yes — retention is configurable at the workspace level. Legal hold is supported: you can pin exports or enable an indefinite retention flag for specific datasets. We'll document the API calls for legal hold and retention overrides in the spec.

Action items: 
- I will complete the questionnaire answers for the security section and return the file by EOD Thursday (Jul 23).
- Aditya will run a short demo of the audit log export and the SIEM streaming integration — propose Wed Jul 22, 10:00am PT (30 min). Aditya, are you available?
- If SOC 2 artifacts are required sooner, Neha (our compliance lead) can share the interim evidence bundle (scope, controls matrix, prep docs) under an NDA.

I'll attach the completed questionnaire and the short demo recording after the call. Let me know if Wed 22 works and if Acme prefers a specific SIEM (Splunk / Sumo Logic / Datadog).

Best,
